bridge: Builds on N02 routing, N05 DNS, N06 redirects and S01 trust boundaries. This is a synthetic URL-policy exercise, with no requests to internal services.
teaching:
SSRF occurs when an application makes a request chosen or influenced by an untrusted caller and crosses an unintended network trust boundary. A server may reach resources the caller cannot reach directly. Returning only a small part of the response does not remove the ability to trigger an action or observe timing.

Prefer selecting from known destinations rather than accepting arbitrary URLs. A URL policy must consider scheme, parsed host/port, DNS resolution, redirects and the final connection destination. Checking a substring such as “trusted.example” is not equivalent to matching the actual hostname.

Network egress restrictions complement application checks. Apply limits to response size, time, redirect count and credential forwarding. If a permitted host redirects, validate the next hop under the same policy instead of assuming the first approval covers the entire chain. Use official cloud guidance for metadata-service protections rather than experimenting against real metadata endpoints.
example:
Synthetic allowlist: https://docs.example on port443, no redirects
A: https://docs.example/help       -> allow
B: https://docs.example.evil.example/help -> deny
C: http://docs.example/help        -> deny scheme
D: https://docs.example:444/help    -> deny port
E: allowed A redirects elsewhere   -> reject redirect under this policy
explanation: The host in B is the longer name ending evil.example, not docs.example. Parsing separates scheme, authority and path; string containment does not. This fixture assumes destination resolution is also constrained by a separate egress policy, which must be verified in a real deployment.
exercise: Classify all five supplied cases and add https://other.example/docs.example as a sixth. Explain which component of each URL determines the allowlist comparison.
solution: Only A is allowed; the sixth is denied because its host is other.example. A path containing an allowed name does not change the destination authority.
challenge: Design a link-preview service supporting only two fixed documentation hosts. State redirect, timeout, size, credential and egress policies. Give a negative case for each boundary without making network requests.
challenge_solution: A defensible design validates every hop, restricts destination/network reachability, forwards no user secrets, caps work and treats parser/connection errors as failure. Name matching alone is not complete SSRF protection.
